nodes.name: Diffusion model (reverse process)
nodes.statement: A diffusion model is a latent variable model $p_\theta(\bx_0) \defeq \int p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})\, d\bx_{1:T}$ whose joint, the reverse process, is a Markov chain $p_\theta(\bx_{0:T}) = p(\bx_T)\prod_{t=1}^T p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)$ with learned Gaussian transitions $p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t) = \mathcal{N}(\bx_{t-1};\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t),\bSigma_\theta(\bx_t,t))$ starting at $p(\bx_T)=\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A diffusion model is a latent-variable model whose joint distribution (the reverse process) is a Markov chain of learned Gaussian transitions starting from a standard-normal prior.

nodes.name: Forward (diffusion) process
nodes.statement: The approximate posterior $q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)\defeq\prod_{t=1}^T q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})$ with $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1}) = \mathcal{N}(\bx_t;\sqrt{1-\beta_t}\,\bx_{t-1},\beta_t\bI)$ is a fixed Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise according to a variance schedule $\beta_1,\dotsc,\beta_T$.
nodes.statement_clean: The forward process is a fixed Markov chain that adds Gaussian noise step-by-step according to a variance schedule.

nodes.name: Notation $\alpha_t,\bar\alpha_t$
nodes.statement: Set $\alpha_t \defeq 1-\beta_t$ and $\bar\alpha_t \defeq \prod_{s=1}^t \alpha_s$.

nodes.name: Discrete reverse-process decoder $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$
nodes.section: 3.3 Data scaling and reverse process decoder
nodes.statement: $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1) = \prod_{i=1}^D \int_{\delta_-(x_0^i)}^{\delta_+(x_0^i)} \mathcal{N}(x;\mu_\theta^i(\bx_1,1),\sigma_1^2)\,dx$ with bin endpoints $\delta_\pm(x)$ extending to $\pm\infty$ at the image-range boundaries; ensures the variational bound is a lossless codelength of discrete pixel data.

nodes.name: $\bepsilon$-prediction parameterization
nodes.statement: Parameterize the reverse-process mean as $\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}\!\left(\bx_t - \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)\right)$, where $\bepsilon_\theta$ is a function approximator predicting the noise $\bepsilon$ from $\bx_t$.

nodes.name: Variational bound on NLL
nodes.statement: $\E[-\log p_\theta(\bx_0)] \le \Eb{q}{-\log p(\bx_T) - \sum_{t\ge 1}\log\frac{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})}} =: L$.

nodes.name: KL-decomposed variational bound
nodes.statement: $L = \E_q\!\left[\underbrace{\kl{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}{p(\bx_T)}}_{L_T} + \sum_{t>1}\underbrace{\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}}_{L_{t-1}} \underbrace{-\log p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)}_{L_0}\right]$.

nodes.name: Closed-form forward marginal
nodes.statement: $q(\bx_t|\bx_0) = \mathcal{N}(\bx_t;\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,\bx_0,(1-\bar\alpha_t)\bI)$.

nodes.name: Forward-process posterior $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)$
nodes.statement: $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)=\mathcal{N}(\bx_{t-1};\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0),\tilde\beta_t\bI)$ with $\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0)=\frac{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{t-1}}\beta_t}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\frac{\sqrt{\alpha_t}(1-\bar\alpha_{t-1})}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bx_t$ and $\tilde\beta_t=\frac{1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\beta_t$.

nodes.name: $L_{t-1}$ as $\bepsilon$-prediction MSE
nodes.statement: $L_{t-1}-C = \Eb{\bx_0,\bepsilon}{\frac{\beta_t^2}{2\sigma_t^2\alpha_t(1-\bar\alpha_t)}\big\|\bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\big\|^2}$.

nodes.name: Simplified training objective $L_{\mathrm{simple}}$
nodes.statement: $L_{\mathrm{simple}}(\theta) \defeq \Eb{t,\bx_0,\bepsilon}{\big\|\bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\big\|^2}$ with $t\sim\mathrm{Unif}\{1,\dotsc,T\}$.

nodes.name: Alternate variational bound (autoregressive form)
nodes.statement: $L = \kl{q(\bx_T)}{p(\bx_T)} + \E_q\!\left[\sum_{t\ge 1} \kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}\right] + H(\bx_0)$.

nodes.name: Progressive estimate $\hat\bx_0$
nodes.statement: $\hat\bx_0 = (\bx_t - \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\,\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t))/\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}$.

nodes.name: Equivalence: $\bepsilon$-prediction VB equals denoising score matching
nodes.statement: Under the parameterization $\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t - \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t))$, the per-step variational bound term $L_{t-1}$ equals (up to a $t$-dependent weight) a denoising score matching loss $\E\|\bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)\|^2$, so VB training matches a Langevin-like sampler to the data via variational inference.
conclusions: Optimizing this objective is equivalent to fitting a Langevin-like sampling chain by variational inference.

nodes.name: Reduced-variance KL decomposition of $L$
nodes.statement: The variational bound $L = \Eb{q}{-\log p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})/q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)}$ admits the closed-form decomposition $L = \E_q[\,L_T + \sum_{t>1} L_{t-1} + L_0\,]$ with $L_T,L_{t-1}$ KL divergences between Gaussians and $L_0=-\log p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$.
assumptions: Forward process $q$ is a Gaussian Markov chain (DP230.2)
conclusions: All KL terms are between Gaussians and admit closed-form (Rao-Blackwellized) evaluation.

nodes.name: Diffusion as generalized autoregressive model
nodes.statement: If $T = D$ (data dimension) and the forward process masks one new coordinate per step with $p(\bx_T)$ a point mass on a blank image, then minimizing $\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}$ trains $p_\theta$ to copy unmasked coordinates and predict the next coordinate, which is exactly autoregressive training; hence the Gaussian diffusion is an autoregressive model with a generalized bit ordering not expressible by reordering coordinates.
assumptions: $q(\bx_t|\bx_0)$ places all mass on $\bx_0$ with first $t$ coordinates masked
$p(\bx_T)$ is a point mass on a blank image
conclusions: Training on the alternate VB EP230.7 reduces to training an autoregressive model coordinate-by-coordinate.

nodes.name: Training (DDPM)
nodes.statement: Sample $(\bx_0,t,\bepsilon)$, then take a gradient step on $\|\bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,\,t)\|^2$ until convergence.
nodes.pseudocode: repeat: $\bx_0\sim q(\bx_0)$; $t\sim\mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dots,T\}$; $\bepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$; gradient step on $\nabla_\theta \|\bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\|^2$; until converged.

nodes.name: Sampling (DDPM)
nodes.statement: Starting from $\bx_T\sim\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$, iteratively denoise via $\bx_{t-1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t - \frac{1-\alpha_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)) + \sigma_t \bz$ for $t=T,\dots,1$, returning $\bx_0$.

nodes.name: Sending $\bx_0$ (progressive lossy code)
nodes.statement: Send $\bx_T\sim q(\bx_T|\bx_0)$ using $p(\bx_T)$, then for $t=T-1,\dots,1$ send $\bx_t\sim q(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1},\bx_0)$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$, and finally send $\bx_0$ using $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$; total expected codelength equals $L$.

nodes.name: Receiving (progressive lossy decode)
nodes.statement: Receive $\bx_T$ using $p(\bx_T)$, then for $t=T-1,\dots,0$ receive $\bx_t$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$; return $\bx_0$.
output: Reconstructed $\bx_0$ (with progressive estimates $\hat\bx_0$ available at each step)

nodes.name: High-fidelity image generation with diffusion models
nodes.statement: Train a diffusion probabilistic model that produces high-quality image samples (competitive Inception/FID scores) on natural-image benchmarks such as CIFAR10, CelebA-HQ $256\times 256$, and LSUN.

nodes.name: Unconditional CIFAR10 generation (IS 9.46, FID 3.17)
nodes.statement: Trained on CIFAR10 with $T=1000$ and a linear $\beta_t$ schedule from $10^{-4}$ to $0.02$, the $L_{\mathrm{simple}}$ model achieves Inception Score $9.46\pm 0.11$ and FID $3.17$ (state-of-the-art among unconditional models reported in the paper) with NLL $\le 3.75$ bits/dim.

nodes.name: CelebA-HQ $256\times 256$ samples and interpolations
nodes.statement: Diffusion model trained on CelebA-HQ $256\times 256$ produces high-quality samples and supports latent-space interpolations $\bar\bx_t=(1-\lambda)\bx_t+\lambda\bx'_t$ that smoothly vary pose, skin tone, hair, expression, and background, with coarser variation as the diffusion depth $t$ grows.

nodes.name: LSUN $256\times 256$ Bedroom/Church/Cat samples
nodes.statement: On LSUN $256\times 256$, the $L_{\mathrm{simple}}$ model attains FID $6.36$ (Bedroom; $4.90$ for the larger model), $7.89$ (Church), and $19.75$ (Cat), comparable to ProgressiveGAN/StyleGAN baselines.

nodes.name: Rate-distortion on CIFAR10 test set
nodes.statement: Treating $L_1+\dots+L_T$ as rate and $L_0$ as distortion gives rate $1.78$ bits/dim and distortion $1.97$ bits/dim (RMSE $0.95/255$); the rate-distortion curve drops steeply at low rate, showing most bits encode imperceptible distortions.

nodes.name: Progressive generation of $\hat\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Running AP230.2 and reading off $\hat\bx_0$ at each step shows large-scale image features appearing first and fine details last, consistent with conceptual compression.

nodes.name: Choice of $\bSigma_\theta=\sigma_t^2\bI$ (untrained)
nodes.statement: Setting $\sigma_t^2=\beta_t$ and $\sigma_t^2=\tilde\beta_t$ both yield similar empirical results; the two are optimal endpoints corresponding to data-distribution upper/lower bounds on reverse-process entropy. Learning a diagonal $\bSigma_\theta$ instead led to unstable training.

nodes.name: $L_T$ is a constant when $\beta_t$ are fixed
nodes.statement: Because $q$ has no learnable parameters in our implementation, $L_T = \kl{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}{\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)} \approx 10^{-5}$ bits/dim is constant during training and ignored.

nodes.name: Limitations of the lossy-compression argument
nodes.statement: AP230.3/AP230.4 are a proof of concept: they rely on minimal random coding, which is not tractable in high dimensions, so they constitute a compression interpretation of the variational bound rather than a deployable codec.

nodes.name: Differences from NCSN
nodes.statement: Vs. NCSN: U-Net with self-attention (not RefineNet), per-layer time conditioning via sinusoidal embedding, $\sqrt{1-\beta_t}$ scaling so variance does not grow, very small $\beta_t$ ensuring forward-process reversibility, and Langevin-like sampler coefficients derived from the forward process rather than tuned by hand.

nodes.name: Derivation of the KL-decomposed VB (Proposition PrP230.2)
nodes.statement: Algebraic re-grouping of $L = \E_q[-\log p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})/q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)]$ using $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})=q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)q(\bx_t|\bx_0)/q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_0)$ yields the KL decomposition.

nodes.name: Expand $L$ as a sum of log-ratios
nodes.statement: Write $L = \E_q[-\log p(\bx_T) - \sum_{t\ge 1}\log\frac{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})}]$ by substituting the chain factorizations of $p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})$ and $q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)$.

nodes.name: Split off the $t=1$ term
nodes.statement: Separate the $t=1$ contribution as $-\log\frac{p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)}{q(\bx_1|\bx_0)}$ and group the $t>1$ terms.

nodes.name: Apply Bayes' rule for the conditioned forward posterior
nodes.statement: Use $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1}) = q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1},\bx_0) = q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0) q(\bx_t|\bx_0)/q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_0)$ inside each $t>1$ log-ratio.

nodes.name: Telescope the marginal ratios
nodes.statement: The product $\prod_{t>1} q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_0)/q(\bx_t|\bx_0)$ telescopes, leaving $q(\bx_1|\bx_0)/q(\bx_T|\bx_0)$, which combines with the $-\log p(\bx_T)$ term and the split-off $t=1$ term.

nodes.name: Identify KL divergences and conclude
nodes.statement: Recognize the resulting expectations as $\kl{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}{p(\bx_T)} + \sum_{t>1}\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)} - \log p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$, which is EP230.2.

nodes.name: Derivation of Equation EP230.5 ($\bepsilon$-form of $L_{t-1}$) and Proposition PrP230.1
nodes.statement: Starting from the Gaussian KL closed form $L_{t-1} = \Eb{q}{\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\|\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0) - \bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t)\|^2}+C$, reparameterize $\bx_t=\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon$, simplify $\tilde\bmu_t$, then substitute the $\bepsilon$-prediction parameterization to obtain the noise-prediction MSE.

nodes.name: KL between Gaussians gives mean-difference squared
nodes.statement: Since $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)$ and $p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)$ are both Gaussian with covariance $\sigma_t^2\bI$, $L_{t-1}=\Eb{q}{\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\|\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0)-\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t)\|^2}+C$.

nodes.name: Reparameterize $\bx_t$ via $\bepsilon$
nodes.statement: Use the closed form $q(\bx_t|\bx_0)$ to write $\bx_t(\bx_0,\bepsilon)=\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon$ for $\bepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Express $\tilde\bmu_t$ in terms of $(\bx_t,\bepsilon)$
nodes.statement: Substitute $\bx_0 = (\bx_t-\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon)/\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}$ in $\tilde\bmu_t$ and simplify to $\tilde\bmu_t = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t-\frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon)$.

nodes.name: Adopt $\bepsilon$-prediction parameterization
nodes.statement: Choose $\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t-\frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t))$ so the difference $\tilde\bmu_t-\bmu_\theta = \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}(\bepsilon_\theta-\bepsilon)$.

nodes.name: Collect and conclude $\bepsilon$-MSE form
nodes.statement: Squaring and pulling out constants gives $L_{t-1}-C = \Eb{\bx_0,\bepsilon}{\frac{\beta_t^2}{2\sigma_t^2\alpha_t(1-\bar\alpha_t)}\|\bepsilon-\bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\|^2}$, matching denoising score matching weighted by $\beta_t^2/(2\sigma_t^2\alpha_t(1-\bar\alpha_t))$.

nodes.name: Derivation of alternate VB EP230.7
nodes.statement: Replace $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})$ by $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)q(\bx_{t-1})/q(\bx_t)$ inside $L$, telescope the marginal ratios down to $q(\bx_0)$, and rewrite $-\E[\log q(\bx_0)]=H(\bx_0)$.

nodes.name: Bayes-rule rewrite of forward conditionals
nodes.statement: Use $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1}) = q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)\,q(\bx_t)/q(\bx_{t-1})$ in each summand of $L$.

nodes.name: Telescope marginal ratios
nodes.statement: The product $\prod_{t\ge 1} q(\bx_{t-1})/q(\bx_t)$ collapses to $q(\bx_0)/q(\bx_T)$, giving $L = \E_q[-\log p(\bx_T)/q(\bx_T) - \sum_{t\ge 1}\log p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)/q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t) - \log q(\bx_0)]$.

nodes.name: Identify KLs and entropy and conclude
nodes.statement: Read off $\kl{q(\bx_T)}{p(\bx_T)}$, $\sum_{t\ge 1}\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}$, and $H(\bx_0)$, yielding EP230.7.

nodes.name: Sample data, timestep, noise
nodes.statement: $\bx_0\sim q(\bx_0)$; $t\sim\mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dotsc,T\}$; $\bepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Take gradient step on $L_{\mathrm{simple}}$
nodes.statement: Update $\theta$ along $\nabla_\theta\|\bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,\,t)\|^2$.

nodes.name: Repeat until convergence
nodes.statement: Iterate steps 1-2 until the loss converges.

nodes.name: Initialize $\bx_T$ from prior
nodes.statement: $\bx_T \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Reverse-process loop $t=T,\dots,1$
nodes.statement: For each $t$, draw $\bz\sim\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$ if $t>1$ else $\bz=\bzero$ and update $\bx_{t-1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t - \frac{1-\alpha_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)) + \sigma_t\bz$.

nodes.name: Return $\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Return the final $\bx_0$.

nodes.name: Send $\bx_T$ using prior
nodes.statement: Send $\bx_T \sim q(\bx_T|\bx_0)$ using $p(\bx_T)$ via minimal random coding.

nodes.name: Loop $t=T-1,\dots,1$ sending intermediate $\bx_t$
nodes.statement: For each $t$, send $\bx_t \sim q(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1},\bx_0)$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$.

nodes.name: Send $\bx_0$ via discrete decoder
nodes.statement: Send $\bx_0$ using $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$ (the discretized Gaussian decoder DP230.4).

nodes.name: Receive $\bx_T$
nodes.statement: Receive $\bx_T$ using $p(\bx_T)$.

nodes.name: Loop receiving $\bx_t$
nodes.statement: For $t=T-1,\dots,0$, receive $\bx_t$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$. At each $t$, the receiver may form the progressive estimate $\hat\bx_0$ via EP230.8.

nodes.name: Return $\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Return $\bx_0$.

nodes.name: Diffusion probabilistic model (Sohl-Dickstein et al., 2015)
nodes.statement: Existence of a learnable Gaussian Markov chain that reverses a fixed Gaussian-noise diffusion process and admits a tractable variational lower bound on the log-likelihood.

nodes.name: Denoising score matching with annealed Langevin dynamics (NCSN)
nodes.statement: Score matching $\bs_\theta(\bx,\sigma)$ over multiple noise scales $\sigma$ trains a noise-conditional score network that, combined with annealed Langevin dynamics, produces high-quality samples.
